description: A delay modelled on the Binson Echorec: a spinning magnetic disc recorded by one head, read by six play heads in turn and then wiped by an erase head. Delays run from 4ms to 6583ms

params.text: Sets the speed of the disc in centimetres per second, which sets the delay of all six play heads together; 12 cm/s is about one turn of the disc per second
Scales the signal entering the module, 0 to 2.00x, default 1.00x
Switches that play head on and off; with it off that head reads nothing from the disc
Moves that play head around the disc, shortening or lengthening its own delay while the others stay put
Switches the erase head on and off; with it off the disc records over itself and earlier passes stay on it, which is what SWELL then controls
Sets the level of that play head, from silent to louder than the dry signal, at both its tap out and the main outputs
Scales the signal at both outputs, 0 to 2.00x, default 1.00x
Works as a feedback control while the erase head is off, running from no repeats beyond the first to endless ones
Balances the input against the delayed signal; at either end of its travel only one of the two is heard
Sets how strongly the input is recorded onto the disc; at high settings the erase head leaves faint repeats behind even while it is on
Tap it in time and the disc speed is set from the interval between the taps
Wipes the whole disc at once, so everything recorded on it stops repeating
Slows the disc by ten, taking its slowest speed down to 0.1 cm/s and the longest delay out to about 55 seconds
Attenuates the voltage at the CV input before it reaches the disc speed

inputs.text: Each gate or trigger switches that play head between on and off
Takes a processed copy of that play head back into the chain
Each gate or trigger switches the erase head between on and off
Gates or triggers here set the disc speed from the interval between them, which syncs the delay to a clock
A voltage from 0 to +10V changing the speed of the disc, scaled by the CV knob
A gate slows the disc down to a stop, as pressing a finger onto the disc would

outputs.text: The left side of the delayed signal
Carries that play head on its own, for processing it outside the module
The right side of the delayed signal

notes: the magic eye display reads the incoming level, and its two wings meeting in the centre means the signal is clipping
each play head has a display showing the delay that head is currently reading at, in ms
the six play heads are spaced one twelfth of a turn apart, so at the standard disc speed they read at 83ms, 166ms, 250ms, 333ms, 416ms and 500ms
